### Observed differences

- Activity A02 was not observed in any of the 200 earlier traces. In the later window it occurs exactly once in every trace (participation 100 in 100, mean 1.0 occurrence per trace, no repetitions). [OCC001]
- In the later window, A02 sits early in the case: its median position is about one-third of the way through the trace, with the middle half of its positions falling between roughly one-sixth and one-half. [POS001]
- New connections form around A02. In the later window, A01 leads to A02 in about 24 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions (previously never), as do A03 (about 24 in 100) and A06 (about 18 in 100); A02 itself leads to all six other activities, most often A04 (about 26 in 100) and A06 (about 25 in 100). The older outgoing shares shrink accordingly, e.g. A01 to A04 from about 36 to 19 in 100. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- A02's relations with the main activities flip from never co-occurring to co-occurring in every trace, in mixed orders: with A01, A01 comes first in about 56 in 100 traces and A02 first in about 45 in 100; with A03, A03 first in about 55 in 100; with A04, A02 first in about 69 in 100; with A06, roughly even (about 51 vs 49 in 100). [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]
- The step distance between A01 and A04, A03 and A04, and A06 and A04 spreads out in the later window: each pair gains a four-step share (about 23, 15 and 20 in 100 respectively) that was absent before, while one- and two-step gaps become less common. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- For context, 13 control-flow items qualified across the 29 tested units, versus roughly 0.14 items expected by chance in an unchanged process. [screening]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A02 became a new step in the process: unobserved in the earlier window, it is executed exactly once in every later case, typically in the first half of the trace, and is loosely ordered among the existing activities A01, A03, A04, A05, A06 and A07 — it both precedes and follows A01, A03, A04 and A06 in substantial shares, with new edges from A01, A03 and A06 into A02 and outgoing edges from A02 to all six other activities. The wider step distances between A01/A03/A06 and A04 fit A02 being placed between them in some cases. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

The change is observed directly on participation, edges, co-occurrence and position, and all 13 items point to the same underlying difference, a set many times larger than the chance expectation, so sampling variation alone cannot explain it. [OCC001, DIR002, REL001, screening]

Limitations: the items largely restate one underlying difference rather than confirming it independently; the mixed before/after orders show A02 has no fixed slot, so its exact placement varies case by case; and the evidence cannot rule out that A02 already existed as a rarely exercised path that simply was not taken in the earlier sample, since zero participation only means it was not observed there. [OCC001, REL001, REL003]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 29 units tested, 13 items qualified, 0.14 expected without change. 13 items is many times larger than 0.14 — so the count cannot be explained by chance. All items are control-flow family. No time or resource items, so I should not discuss time or resources.

Now let's understand the evidence:

OCC001: A02 — before: mean occurrences per trace 0.0, participation 0.0 (support before 0). After: mean 1.0, participation 1.0 (support after 200). So A02 was absent in the earlier window and appears in every trace in the later window, exactly once per trace (mean 1.0, recurrence support 0 — so no repeats). This is a new activity added, executed once in every case.

DIR001: A01's outgoing transitions. Before: A04 ~36%, A06 ~29%, A03 ~22%, A05 ~7%, A07 ~5%. After: A02 ~24%, A04 ~19%, A03 ~24%, A05 ~7%, A06 ~22%, A07 ~5%. So A01 now sometimes leads to A02 (~24% of its outgoing transitions), with the other shares slightly reduced. Note A01→A02 is a new edge.

DIR002: A02's outgoing transitions. Before: empty (A02 not observed). After: A04 ~26%, A06 ~25%, A01 ~19%, A03 ~19%, A05 ~4%, A07 ~7%. So A02 leads to all the other activities. Support after 189.

DIR003: A03's outgoing. Before: A06 25%, A04 27%, A01 29%, A05 7%, A07 12%. After: A02 24%, A06 20%, A04 24%, A01 20%, A05 5%, A07 7%. So A03 now leads to A02 in ~24% of its outgoing transitions.

DIR004: A06's outgoing. Before: A01 31%, A03 30%, A05 5%, A07 11%, A04 23%. After: A01 24%, A03 26%, A04 19%, A07 7%, A02 18%, A05 5%. So A06 now leads to A02 in ~18%.

POS001: A02 position. Before: no support. After: mean position ~0.37 of the trace (normalized position presumably), median 0.33, q25 0.17, q75 0.5. So A02 occurs early-to-middle in traces.

REL001: A01–A02. Before: A_only = 1.0 (A01 present, A02 absent in all traces), cooccurrence 0. After: cooccurrence 1.0; A_before_B 0.555, B_before_A 0.445. So A01 and A02 now co-occur in all traces, with A01 before A02 in ~56% and A02 before A01 in ~44% — mixed order, no fixed order.

REL002: A02–A03. Before: B_only = 1.0 (A03 present, A02 absent). After: cooccurrence 1.0; A_before_B (A02 before A03) 0.45, B_before_A 0.55. Mixed order.

REL003: A02–A04. Before: B_only 1.0. After: cooccurrence 1.0; A02 before A04 0.685, A04 before A02 0.315. Mixed order, leaning A02 first.

REL004: A02–A06. Before: B_only 1.0. After: cooccurrence 1.0; A02 before A06 0.505, A06 before A02 0.495. Mixed order.

LAG001: A01–A04 lag. Before: lag 1 ~47%, lag 2 ~29%, lag 3 ~23%. After: lag 1 ~26%, lag 2 ~26%, lag 3 ~26%, lag 4 ~23%. So the distance between A01 and A04 spread out, more cases at lag 4. This is consistent with A02 being inserted between them sometimes — inserting an activity between A01 and A04 increases their separation in some traces.

LAG002: A03–A04. Before: lag 1 38%, 2 36%, 3 26%. After: 1 31%, 2 28%, 3 26%, 4 15%. Similar spread.

LAG003: A06–A04. Before: 1 33%, 2 41%, 3 26%. After: 1 25%, 2 34%, 3 21%, 4 20%. Similar.

Interpretation: A02 is a new activity that appears exactly once in every trace in the later window, positioned early (median normalized position ~0.33), and it connects to/from all the main activities: A01→A02 in ~24% of A01's outgoing transitions, A02→{A01, A03, A04, A05, A06, A07}, A03→A02 ~24%, A06→A02 ~18%. The REL items show A02 co-occurs with A01, A03, A04, A06 in every trace, in mixed orders (both orders occur in similar proportions). The LAG items show the distance between A01/A03/A06 and A04 spread out, with a new lag-4 component — consistent with A02 being inserted somewhere in between in some traces.

So the main hypothesis: A02 was added to the process as a new step executed once per case, placed early in the flow, with flexible ordering relative to the existing activities (it can occur before or after A01, A03, A04, A06). This is a structural change: an activity added.

Wait — but is it "added" or was it always there but never observed? Zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window. But with 200 traces before and 0 participation, and 200 after with participation 1.0, the natural reading is that A02 became part of every case. Here we have 13 items, all control-flow, all pointing at A02's emergence and its relational integration. The change is directly observed (participation 0 → 100%, new edges, cooccurrence 0 → 100%). Also note: this is not a "shift in path frequencies" — it's an activity added/becoming mandatory.
